environment.description: Application deployed on EKS (Kubernetes 1.28) behind an internal NLB. Pod spec mounts a PKCS#11 volume from AWS CloudHSM cluster (cloudhsm-client sidecar, firmware version 3.4.4). The init container invokes pkcs11-tool to extract a session-bound HMAC key handle (CKA_EXTRACTABLE=false, CKA_SENSITIVE=true) and exports only the 64-char hex handle reference as CACHE_SIGNING_KEY env var via a Kubernetes projected volume from a sealed-secret. Additionally, an Istio VirtualService with a consistent-hash load balancing policy normalizes the Host header to the mesh-internal service FQDN (cache-app.prod.svc.cluster.local) before traffic reaches the pod, and an Istio AuthorizationPolicy restricts the source principal to only the ingress gateway's SPIFFE identity. The ingress gateway itself has an EnvoyFilter that strips and rewrites the Host header to the canonical service name, and drops requests where X-Forwarded-Host differs from the configured canonical host. The combination means: (1) the signing key is a non-extractable HSM handle so cache integrity is cryptographically enforced even if an attacker can trigger cache writes, and (2) the Host header is always normalized before reaching the app, collapsing the cache-key space so that attacker-controlled Host values never reach computeCacheKey().

config.hsm: AWS CloudHSM cluster, PKCS#11 provider, CKA_EXTRACTABLE=false
config.service_mesh: Istio 1.20, strict mTLS, VirtualService with consistent-hash LB
config.envoy_filter: Host header rewrite to canonical FQDN, X-Forwarded-Host validation
config.authorization_policy: source principal restricted to ingress-gateway SPIFFE ID
config.network: Private subnet, no direct internet access to pods
config.sealed_secret: bitnami sealed-secrets v0.24, HSM key handle as env var
